html:
Waymaq is the name the map gives to a small territory on the upper Sacramento and McCloud rivers, just south of Mount Shasta in northern California. This was the northern edge of the Wintu world, where Wintu-speaking bands met the Shasta and the small Okwanuchu people.

Little is recorded about a group under this exact name. The people of this area fished the salmon runs of the McCloud River and gathered acorns. The Gold Rush of the 1850s brought miners and killings, and in the 1940s Shasta Dam flooded much of the river valley. See also Northern Wintu.
